Class GeoProjection

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.widgets.map.GeoProjection
public final class GeoProjection extends Object
Immutable equirectangular (plate carrée) projection of a MapViewport onto a terminal rectangle, correcting for the proportions of a terminal cell.

A character cell is about twice as tall as it is wide, so filling the whole rectangle with a fixed viewport would stretch the map horizontally. Instead, the requested viewport is treated as the region that must stay visible and is expanded on its shorter axis to match the rectangle's aspect ratio (see effectiveViewport()). The map then fills the rectangle with no distortion and no wasted margin, showing a little more geography. Only when the expansion would exceed the whole globe (360 by 180 degrees) does the map area letterbox. It is plate carrée, not Mercator, so it is for overviews, not local navigation.

The projection converts geographic coordinates to buffer columns and rows and back, so the same transform drives rendering, marker placement, mouse hit-testing and pan/zoom.
